what: The d=1024 step after the shape-dependent library choice: per-category profile, paired canonical/library step, the kernel shape table that sets the threshold, and the gradient equivalence case.

step.row_rule: operator ns divided by 16 rounds; the step's own wall_per_round_ns is the median of the 13 timed steps
step.note: The library changes the gradients, not the forward attention: forward matmul is 941.2 against 859.7 ms, inside the run-to-run spread. grad_lhs falls 1119.3 -> 672.6 ms and grad_rhs 781.3 -> 695.1 ms. The pair is two programs alternating on one host, not one process: tensor::fuse is a whole-program pass.

kernel_shape_pairs.method: one process, #strict canonical and default library functions interleaved per iteration, median of 10 after 2 warmup, one thread, sum forcing the product

rows_ms.path: canonical (both sides run the canonical kernel after the guard)
canonical (both sides run the canonical kernel after the guard)

pre_guard_small.note: These two rows are the raw library before the guard; they are why the threshold exists.

threshold.rule: M*N*K >= 2^30 uses the library; below it sgemmLibrary calls the canonical kernel
threshold.why: the measured crossover is between 1.3e8 (batched attention) and 1.1e9 (1024^3); 2^30 is the measured large side and the batched attention product is decided per call

gradient_equivalence.note: The default gradient really runs the library (diff is not zero); safe mode is bit-identical. This is the backward counterpart of gemm_library.cml.

commands.profile_library: camel -t 1 --block-limit 8192 train_step_1024.cml tensor::fuse 'std::profile top=0 json="prof-1024-lib-a.json" report=true' std::jit --arg bench=true --arg init_dir= --arg final_dir=
commands.paired_sweep: python /tmp/h281-prof/pair_sweep.py (alternates canonical and library per round)
